localChanges: Replaces upstream's tracker-agnostic prose with a deterministic Forgejo adapter and an offline test suite; the skill body no longer carries API instructions that drift.
Requires a private tracker and refuses a repository the API reports as public — several of Bryan's repositories on the same host are public.
Requires the tracker be chosen explicitly alongside the origin remote; it is never inferred.
Every mutation previews by default and needs an explicit apply after Bryan sees the exact content.
Map parentage is a managed metadata block, because Forgejo 16.0.1 has no sub-issue endpoint; blocking uses native issue dependencies.

Arbitrates claims by Forgejo's monotonic comment id, not by body overwrite: claim and release are append-only comments replayed in id order, and the earliest unreleased operation wins. `updated_at` is *set by* the write on this API, so it can only guard staleness — it cannot decide a race.

Claims are bound to an ownership **identity tuple** `(operation, session)`, not a single token: session alone is not ownership (one session runs nested or concurrent operations) and operation alone is not ownership either (every id is written into a tracker comment, so anyone who can read the issue can quote it back; an id is a handle, not a credential).

Never edits any issue body after creation. Forgejo exposes no compare-and-swap or transaction on issue update, so a body PATCH can always overwrite a human edit that lands between the adapter's last read and its write; no client-side lock or readback closes that window. Every piece of adapter-owned state is therefore append-only — created issues and created comments — and the map's decision index is the deterministic replay of exact-schema `index` comments on the map (comment-id order, first record per resolution key), never a section of the body. Concurrent resolutions append two records and cannot overwrite each other or Bryan; there is no map lock, no lock recovery, and no held state a crashed session can leave behind.

Resolution idempotency and indexing are bound to one map, one ticket, one key, one normalized answer: the resolution key digests (map, ticket, answer), the index record carries the key plus the exact ticket and gist, and replay's first-record-per-key rule makes a reworded retry converge on one entry while an identical gist for another ticket can never satisfy this one.

A crash-interrupted claim is surfaced for explicit recovery — never expired or stolen — because a holder that looks abandoned may be mid-write; `release` (with the exact operation and session) is the named recovery path and reaches a queued acquisition as well as the current holder, verifying the winner is untouched.

Managed records have exact per-kind v1 schemas (claim/release: session, operation, at; resolution: session, key, map; index: session, key, map, ticket, gist, at). A block with a malformed line, duplicate key, unknown key, missing key, empty value, wrong version, or out-of-pattern value is discarded whole — it can neither arbitrate nor satisfy readback, idempotency, or the index replay. Rendering shares the same schemas, so the adapter cannot emit a record its own reader would reject.

Nonpositive server ids never cross an identity or arbitration boundary: a record carried by a comment id below 1 has no position in the replay order and is discarded, a comment POST whose echo lacks a positive id fails its readback, and a create that returns issue number 0 or below is a failed create.

A resolution is reported successful only when an index record with its exact key replays on the map; anything else returns explicit retry guidance, and re-running the same resolve performs only the steps that did not land.

Readback is exact per write family, and measured against a pre-write snapshot: a created issue must be a positive number that did not exist before, with byte-exact title, body, and label set; a comment record must be a comment absent from the snapshot, under the positive id the API returned, with a byte-exact body; an assignment must equal the requested set; a dependency must equal the snapshot plus the one requested edge. Without the snapshots, an echoed existing issue or an earlier attempt's record passes as proof of a write that never happened.
Adds a when-this-is-the-wrong-tool section, so a small effort is not charted as a map.
Adds an explicit handoff section: the map ends at a Git artifact and normal issue authority.

Folds upstream `prototype` in as a routing reference rather than a skill, mapping SGG interface questions to the existing `dx-target` and `dx-preview` workflows and writing the three general shapes out inline.
A contender that posts a claim and then loses withdraws its own claim record before standing down, so the winner's release cannot silently transfer the ticket to a session that already walked away.
Re-preflights privacy, issue identity, labels, metadata version, map association, and the active claim immediately before *every* resolution write, not once at entry.
Parses resolution markers structurally across all managed blocks in a comment, requiring exact kind, version, key, map, and session — answer prose can never satisfy idempotency or readback.
Validates the map index entry as a single safe line before preview or mutation, so a decision cannot alter the map's section structure.

Every external write goes through one guarded helper, and **privacy is the last network read before the single mutation** — identity, metadata, ownership, and dependency reads all complete first, and the write closure reads nothing. Checking privacy first and then issuing three more reads leaves a window in which the repository goes public while the adapter is still deciding. There is consequently no GET-then-PATCH helper: read preparation and the direct PATCH/POST are separate.
Adds `claim-status`, so the exact operation id holding a ticket — and the command to release it — is inspectable rather than guessable.

Value validation is real rather than shape-matching: ticket and map numbers must be positive integers (Forgejo numbers issues from 1, so zero is a missing value dressed as one, and the synthetic `ticket: 0` fallback is gone), and a timestamp must parse to a real UTC instant — `2026-99-99T99:99:99Z` matches every plausible regex. Blank lines inside a managed block are rejected rather than skipped, because padding a reader tolerates is padding a forger can hide behind.

Map and ticket identity are exact: a map needs exactly one balanced current-version managed region (zero is not a map; two is worse, since a decision would be merged into one while a reader sees the other), and a ticket needs both `wayfinder:ticket` and the `wayfinder:{type}` label agreeing with exact `map`/`type` metadata — a label that contradicts the body is two sources of truth, and this adapter refuses to pick one.

Review lane selection preserves one load-bearing inventory shape: `git diff --name-status -z -M -C --find-copies-harder … --`. The classifier help keeps the generic `{base}...HEAD` template, while `code-review` and `pr-self-review` substitute their immutable base/head SHA pair. `--find-copies-harder` is load-bearing: plain `-C` only inspects modified files, so copying a risky *untouched* source emits a bare `A` and the risky source is never classified. Parsing is strict — a suffixed status, an impossible similarity score, a misaligned empty field, truncation, an empty path, a control character, or undecodable bytes all refuse, because a guess here is a silently narrowed review.

The deterministic selector and its tests live under pr-self-review (scripts/select_review_lanes.py, tests/test_select_review_lanes.py) and are consumed by both code-review and pr-self-review; the Git name-status parser validates exact status bytes before any normalization and rejects every control character in a path, tab included.

Keeps Standards, Spec, and conditional Risk as the primary lane architecture, then runs a mandatory host-independent Ponytail over-engineering quality gate last against every exact candidate. The shared contract is deliberately narrow (delete/YAGNI/stdlib/native/shrink only), requires `review-ponytail.md`, and does not depend on a Claude plugin or slash command.

Pins review artifacts to immutable base, head, merge-base, and binary-diff identities, and distributes `code-review` anywhere `pr-self-review` is curated, including Pi, so no host can receive the orchestrator without its mandatory Ponytail contract.
